title: Our Palace questions suspects after an attack on a family, and hands the case to the gendarmerie
excerpt: After a family home in Guneku was attacked, the community brought the matter to the Palace. Our elders questioned suspects on 2 October 2026 and handed them to the gendarmerie. The suspects have not been tried.
sourceNote: Written fresh on 17 October 2026 from two public community sources — the Fondom Studios documentary (published 5 October 2026, 21:20 UTC) and the Mbengwi Info Newsline post of 2 October 2026 — and from the community intelligence review of the same date, which sampled the documentary's footage and read the village community group. A report that the suspects came from a neighbouring village is unconfirmed and is deliberately not repeated. No photograph is reproduced: the circulating images show the suspects, and the victims are protected. No person is named. Recorded allegations are reported as allegations; no court outcome is established in either source. Rewritten 17 October 2026 in the community's own voice at the owner's direction; the owner decided the mother's disability is not published and the documentary link stays. Claim status is kept in docs (R-072): questioning at the Palace and handover corroborated; 120,000 FCFA and recovered items single-source; the assault an allegation; the attack date and any outcome unknown.
body:
A family home in Guneku was attacked. Two young girls were allegedly assaulted inside the house, and about 120,000 FCFA was reportedly taken from the family. The children are not named here, and nothing that could identify them or their family will be published.

Our Palace and our elders

The family and the community brought the matter to the Guneku Palace. Our elders and traditional institutions gathered information quietly, and suspects were identified. On Friday 2 October 2026 the suspects were brought before the Palace and questioned by the elders, and items were reportedly recovered in the course of the investigation.

The Palace then handed the matter to the State. That same afternoon the suspects were taken by the gendarmerie to Mbengwi for further questioning, and calm returned to the village.

Our community leaders thanked everyone who helped, and asked all of us to stay vigilant, to report suspicious movements to the proper authorities, and never to take the law into our own hands.

Before the courts

The suspects now face the ordinary legal process, and they are presumed innocent until a court decides otherwise. What was said during the questioning at the Palace is not a court finding. No charge, trial or judgment has been announced so far. We will update this page when there is news.

In the days that followed, the men of Fun Quarter performed traditional rites to protect the land: Fun Quarter performs traditional rites to protect the land.

Watch the documentary

Fondom Studios, the Guneku media company, filmed the proceedings at the Palace. Its documentary, published on 5 October 2026, is on Facebook: Guneku ritual vs thieves & rapist suspects — Fondom Studios. The film shows the suspects; Fondom Studios asks viewers not to try to identify the victims. Mbengwi Info Newsline reported the arrest on the day.
